claim: Nepal had 16.5M internet users (55.8% penetration) and 39.0M cellular connections, 80.5% broadband, in Jan 2025.
quoted_support: 16.5 million individuals using the internet in Nepal at the start of 2025, when online penetration stood at 55.8 percent.

claim: MICS 2024/25: 82% of households have internet, urban 86.5% vs rural 73%, Karnali 68.5%.
quoted_support: In Urban areas, 86.5% of the total have access to the internet, while in rural areas, it stood at 73%

claim: Only 19.2% verified information found online and 24.2% could copy/paste files, implying plain-language, low-skill UX is needed.
quoted_support: only 19.2% of those in the survey verified the information they found online

claim: ITU IDI 2026 puts Nepal internet use at 48.4% and household internet at 52.5%, 81.6% 4G coverage; estimates differ from MICS.
quoted_support: 48.4 percent of Nepal's population uses the internet, while 73.1 percent own a mobile phone. Internet access has reached 52.5 percent of households.

claim: Government documents in image/Preeti formats are unreadable to screen readers; 2021 directive requires Unicode, adjustable font sizes, bilingual content.
stance_target: Atlas should use Unicode, tagged HTML/PDF
quoted_support: If content is simply made available in Unicode, it would already make a huge difference for us.

claim: Unicode Nepali is mandated for government info but is found inaccessible when applied in PDF; WCAG AA audit found missing landmarks.
stance_target: printable report PDFs must be tagged accessible
quoted_support: Government offices have made the Unicode system mandatory for the exchange of public information. However, Unicode is found to be inaccessible when it is applied in PDF format.

claim: W3C Devanagari gap analysis flags vowel-sign and conjunct handling problems in browsers, relevant to Nepali text rendering.
quoted_support: all engines have problems with vowel-signs, especially but not only pre-base vowel-signs.
